To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the opsonizing antibody response against FMDV is more broadly reactive than the neutralizing response, and that pDC activation via TLR7 by different isolates of FMDV is highly heterogeneous.

1) the opsonising titres mediating pDC responses were similar to neutralising titres when antigenically related FMDV strains from the same serotypes were employed, but 2) cross-reactivity of sera with non-neutralized FMDV strains of different serotypes was observed and 3) the pDC response to FMDV was strongly influenced by the viral isolate used.

(1) opsonising antibodies against FMDV have a broader specificity than neutralizing antibodies; (2) the opsonising titres are similar to neutralizing antibody titres; (3) opsonising antibody-mediated pDC activation is not dependent on the presence of neutralizing antibodies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay of FMDV, opsonizing and neutralizing antibodies and plasmocytoid dendritic cells and the role that these interactions play in the immune response to infection.
the role of opsonizing antibodies in virus clearance and IFN-α induction and may contribute to the development of novel strategies for the control of viral infections.
the interaction of FMDV with opsonizing antibodies and pDC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

opsonising antibody responses are not only important for the clearance of the virus, but also for the stimulation of IFN-α production in pDC, and therefore, are important in the antiviral immune response.
opsonising and/or non-neutralizing antibody titres are a useful measure for the assessment of the immune response against FMDV and may be of value for the assessment of immune protection.
FMDV opsonization by antibodies results in enhanced type-I interferon responses by pDC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the interaction of FMDV with pDC is complex and that it is dependent on virus and antibody characteristics.
opsonising FMDV-specific antibodies can be a useful tool for the activation of pDC to induce IFN-α production and that this response is dependent on the viral strain used for the assay.

the interaction of FMDV and pDC is more complex than previously assumed and the interplay of FMDV, antibodies and pDC is a dynamic process that may be of relevance for viral clearance and the induction of antiviral responses.
The main takeaway from our work is that

opsonizing antibodies can contribute to virus clearance and the production of type I IFN by pDC, but the magnitude of the response is dependent on virus strain and the presence of neutralizing antibodies.
opsonisation by non-neutralizing antibodies is an important mechanism of immune response contributing to type-I IFN induction by pDC.
opsonizing antibody titres mediate similar responses to neutralizing antibody titres, when the same serotype of virus is tested.
